# Complete L0 Documentation Roadmap

I use this plan to produce complete, in-depth, LLM-friendly documentation for L0.

## Goals

I want this documentation set to let other LLMs (and people) learn and reference L0 end-to-end:
- language abilities and semantics
- command-line abilities and usage
- binary/debug/trace formats
- practical examples and troubleshooting

## Documentation Principles

I follow these rules:
- deterministic structure and headings
- first-person voice
- normative vs informative separation
- canonical, runnable examples
- stable cross-links and section anchors

## Planned Information Architecture

I will maintain these core docs as source of truth in `docs/`:
- `LANGUAGE.md`
- `SPEC.md`
- `IMPLEMENTABLE_SPEC.md`
- `INSTRUCTION_SET.md`
- `WORKFLOWS.md`
- `HOW_TO_WRITE_L0.md`
- contract docs (`*_v1` surfaces)
- status/progress (`STATUS.md`)

I will also maintain a curated mirror in `wiki/` for fast GitHub Wiki-style browsing.

## Dual-Doc Pipeline

I implement a dual-doc pipeline with these constraints:
- `docs/` is canonical source-of-truth
- `wiki/` is generated from `docs/` via deterministic script
- drift between `docs/` and `wiki/` is test-gated

Pipeline components:
- source map: `wiki/SOURCE_MAP.tsv`
- generator: `scripts/sync_wiki.sh`
- gate: `tests/wiki_sync.sh`

## Coverage Program

I will maintain a coverage matrix mapping:
- language ability -> canonical doc section -> runnable example -> test gate
- CLI command/flag -> reference section -> success/failure examples
- error category -> contract doc -> assertion coverage

## Example Program

For each major ability I will include:
- minimal canonical example
- practical example
- failure example with expected deterministic error class

## Validation Gates

I will keep documentation quality enforced in automation:
- link and reference consistency
- generated wiki drift checks
- example sync checks against runnable fixtures

## Phased Execution Plan

1. Create and lock the dual-doc pipeline (`docs` -> `wiki`) and drift gate.
2. Expand language and command reference depth by ability.
3. Add and maintain explicit coverage matrix tables.
4. Extend runnable examples and troubleshooting references.
5. Keep release-candidate docs and wiki mirror synchronized.
6. Freeze final `v1.0.0` docs snapshot with manifest verification.
7. Add machine-readable docs index for deterministic LLM tooling.
8. Add CI wiki autopublish flow for `main` updates.
9. Add governance, security, toolchain, and release-note operations docs.

## Done Definition

I consider this complete when:
- all language and command abilities are documented with examples
- canonical `docs/` and generated `wiki/` are always in sync
- docs quality gates pass in `make test`
- other LLMs can use docs as deterministic reference without ambiguity
